articles.title: Securing the Software Supply Chain: Generating SBOMs & SLSA Provenance in GitLab CI/CD
articles.excerpt: Securing the Software Supply Chain: Generating SBOMs & SLSA Provenance in GitLab CI/CD From the SolarWinds breach to the recent XZ Utils backdoor, software supply chain attacks have moved from theoret…
articles.body: Securing the Software Supply Chain: Generating SBOMs & SLSA Provenance in GitLab CI/CD From the SolarWinds breach to the recent XZ Utils backdoor, software supply chain attacks have moved from theoretical risks to frontline security crises. It is no longer enough to verify that your own proprietary code is clean. Regulators, enterprise buyers, and security frameworks (like NIST SP 800-218 , Executive Order 14028 , and FedRAMP ) now mandate: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) : An exact, machine-readable inventory of every third-party package and transitive dependency shipped inside your binaries and containers. SLSA Build Provenance (Supply-chain Levels for Software Artifacts) : Cryptographic proof of where , when , and by what git commit a binary artifact was compiled.

articles.title: AI Can Build Your React UI in Seconds. What About the Backend?
articles.excerpt: A few weeks ago, I opened Cursor and gave Claude a single prompt: "Generate a modern task management dashboard with filtering, search, pagination, and a modal form to create tasks." In under fifteen s…
articles.body: A few weeks ago, I opened Cursor and gave Claude a single prompt: "Generate a modern task management dashboard with filtering, search, pagination, and a modal form to create tasks." In under fifteen seconds, it delivered hundreds of lines of polished Tailwind JSX, responsive grid layouts, and lucide-react icons. I clicked preview, and my jaw dropped. It looked like something a high-end design agency would spend weeks polishing. Then I tried to actually use it. I filled out the "Create Task" form, clicked submit, and refreshed the browser. Everything vanished. The data immediately reset to the initial dummy state. The AI had done what AI coding tools always do: it stuffed a hardcoded useState([ ... ]) dummy array right at the top of the component.

articles.title: Testing Across Everything: Mastering Matrix Builds & Parallelism in GitLab CI/CD
articles.excerpt: Testing Across Everything: Mastering Matrix Builds & Parallelism in GitLab CI/CD When maintaining an open-source library, cross-platform CLI tool, or multi-tenant backend, you can never assume that co…
articles.body: Testing Across Everything: Mastering Matrix Builds & Parallelism in GitLab CI/CD When maintaining an open-source library, cross-platform CLI tool, or multi-tenant backend, you can never assume that code passing on Node.js 22 or Python 3.12 on Linux will run without errors on Node 18 or Python 3.10 on macOS. Historically, testing multiple versions in CI meant one of two terrible options: The Sequential Slow-Down : Running tests for Python 3.10, then 3.11, then 3.12 one after another inside a single job. A 5-minute test suite turns into a 25-minute crawl. The Copy-Paste YAML Nightmare : Duplicating 40 lines of CI job configuration 6 times with different image tags. Fortunately, GitLab CI/CD features native Parallel Matrix Builds ( parallel: matrix: ).

articles.title: BERT's tokenizer bottleneck was hiding before WordPiece
articles.excerpt: BERT's tokenizer bottleneck was hiding before WordPiece Normalization consumed 88% of a warm English encoding pass with bert-base-uncased. WordPiece, the algorithm that chooses tokens, took 8%. Simon…
articles.body: BERT's tokenizer bottleneck was hiding before WordPiece Normalization consumed 88% of a warm English encoding pass with bert-base-uncased . WordPiece, the algorithm that chooses tokens, took 8%. Simon Brandeis reports those measurements in his October 15 Hugging Face article , which follows the work from a CPU profile to a proposed implementation. The surprising part is where the time went. A tokenizer sounds like a problem about finding token boundaries, yet this profile mostly measured the cost of preparing characters. For an embedding or RAG service, that makes tokenization worth measuring separately from the model. It doesn't establish that tokenization dominates any particular service.

articles.title: 암호화폐의 변혁: 기관 자본이 시장 구조를 어떻게 재편하는가

articles.body: 한때 얼리어답터와 투기적인 개인 투자자들의 틈새 영역에 불과했던 암호화폐 시장은 지금 심오하고 되돌릴 수 없는 변화를 겪고 있다. 분산 금융의 급진적인 실험으로 시작된 이 시장은 이제 상당한 규모의 글로벌 자산군으로 성숙해, 안목 있는 기관 투자자들의 시선과 막대한 자본을 끌어들이고 있다. 이러한 기관 자금의 유입은 단순히 유동성을 더하는 것을 넘어, 암호화폐 생태계의 근본적인 아키텍처, 운영 메커니즘, 그리고 규제 프레임워크를 바꾸고 있다. 이 변화는 시장이 주로 개인 주도적이고 파편화된 초기 단계를 넘어 더욱 전문화되고 통합되며 규제를 준수하는 금융 환경으로 나아가는 중요한 변곡점을 의미한다. 이러한 진화의 규모는 현재 시장의 총 시가총액이 약 2조 7,800억 달러에 달한다는 점에서 더욱 부각된다. 이 수치는 매일 변동될 수 있지만, 디지털 자산이 광범위한 금융 시스템의 합법적인 구성 요소로 인식되고 있음을 보여준다. 헤지펀드, 자산운용사, 기업, 심지어 국부펀드에 이르는 기관 참여는 전통 금융(TradFi)에서 볼 수 있는 것과 유사한 강력한 인프라, 명확한 규제, 그리고 정교한 금융 상품에 대한 수요를 동반한다. 이 글에서는 이러한 기관 자본 유입이 시장 구조를 어떻게 재편하는지, 즉 인프라의 전문화, 유동성 강화, 정교한 파생상품 개발, 그리고 진화하는 규제 환경을 면밀히 살펴보는 동시에, 이러한 통합 과정에 내재된 한계와 잠재적 과제 또한 다룰 것이다. 현재의 변화를 제대로 이해하려면 초기 암호화폐 시장의 태동기적 특성을 파악하는 것이 중요하다.

articles.title: Connected steps are not a workflow
articles.excerpt: Take a task that crosses two apps. A customer asks for a refund. The request lives in the support desk. The order lives in the billing system. End to end, the agent reads both, decides against the ref…
articles.body: Take a task that crosses two apps. A customer asks for a refund. The request lives in the support desk. The order lives in the billing system. End to end, the agent reads both, decides against the refund rules, issues the refund, and confirms back to the customer. The rules are in neither API. Refunds under fifty dollars are fine when the order is paid and never refunded before. Over that, a manager decides. Testimonials wait for a human before they go live. Escalation happens after two contacts. None of that lives in the support desk or the billing system. It lives in the team's heads. Now watch the handoffs. The agent reads the order in billing. Then it moves to the support desk carrying a snapshot of a moment that has already passed. Billing permits the refund under one permission set.

articles.body: Every once in a while, I come across a line that feels bigger than the book that birthed it. articles.title: Rep. Ritchie Torres Introduces Legislation to Ensure Gamers Own Their Digital Games
articles.excerpt: Democratic Congressman Ritchie Torres is introducing legislation that aims to ensure you own your digital games, rather than having a license.
articles.body: Democratic Congressman Ritchie Torres is introducing legislation that aims to ensure you own your digital games, rather than merely buying a license that gives you permission to play them. The bill, known as The Power to the Players Act, would direct the Fedral Trade Commission (FTC) to establish regulations that would protect gamers and their digital libraries. In short, Torres wants to ensure that when you buy a digital game, you actually own it, as opposed to getting a license that can be revoked. Additionally, the bill would require online games to have offline functionality, so that when servers are shut down, the content can still be played by those who own the game.

articles.title: Targeted ads delivered 0-click exploits to install mercenary malware
articles.excerpt: The incident is likely 1st confirmation of mercenary spyware delivered by targeted ads.
articles.body: Researchers say that mercenary hackers laced ads with zero-click exploits that installed sophisticated malware on the devices of targeted individuals when they did nothing other than load a website or open an installed app. The finding, published Thursday by the University of Toronto’s Citizen Lab, said the incident is likely to be the first confirmation of zero-click mercenary spyware delivered through targeted ads. The attacks, which worked on iOS and Android devices, are particularly pernicious because they work without requiring any interaction from the target and are invisible unless users run special forensic hardware or software.

articles.title: Astronomers discover the 1st ever green star, a cosmic zombie just in time for Halloween
articles.excerpt: Imagine if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween. Scientists have discovered that our star may go green if it turns into a cosmic zombie after its death in billions of years.
articles.body: How awesome would it be if the sun could take on a spooky green glow for Halloween? It turns out that scientists have discovered that our star may indeed go green, but only billions of years from now after its death — and only if it then starts eating planets like a cosmic zombie. That's possible because scientists have discovered that white dwarfs, the type of stellar remnants sun-sized stars leave behind when they die, can actually take on a range of colors including green if they snack on their rocky planets like cosmic cannibals. For stellar scientists, the colors of stars have always been indicative of their temperatures. Cool stars look orange, while stars like the sun look white , and the hottest stars glow pale blue.
articles.author: Robert Lea

articles.title: NASA to Help Unlock Mysteries of Mars’ Moons in Upcoming Mission
articles.excerpt: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long his…
articles.body: NASA is playing an important role in JAXA’s (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) MMX (Martian Moons eXploration) mission, to advance our understanding of Mars’ moons and build on the agency’s long history of exploring the Red Planet. The mission aims to characterize and determine the origin of Mars’ moons Phobos and Deimos and deliver a sample of Phobos to Earth. The MMX spacecraft is targeting launch from JAXA’s Tanegashima Space Center in Japan at 3:41 p.m. EDT on Monday, Oct. 19 (4:41 a.m. JST on Tuesday, Oct. 20). An artist’s concept of JAXA’s MMX spacecraft during its Mars’ orbit insertion. The Martian moon Phobos, which MMX will explore and sample, is in the background.

articles.title: On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn
articles.excerpt: On this day in space! Oct. 15, 1997: NASA launches Cassini-Hugyens probe on 7-year voyage to Saturn
articles.body: On Oct. 15, 1997, NASA launched the Cassini spacecraft on a mission to explore Saturn and its moons. It lifted off aboard a Titan 4B rocket from Cape Canaveral Air Force Station in Florida. It took almost seven years for the Cassini spacecraft to reach Saturn , with the spacecraft entering orbit around the ringed planet in 2004. Another smaller spacecraft called Huygens hitched a ride with Cassini, and it landed on Saturn's moon Titan in 2005. Cassini spent 13 years studying the Saturn system up close, and the mission lasted about 20 years before coming to an epic grand finale on Sept. 15, 2017 . articles.title: SpaceX launches classified mission for the US Space Force (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California this evening (Oct. 15), on the 114th Falcon 9 mission of the year.
articles.body: SpaceX launched a classified mission for the U.S. Space Force from California this evening (Oct. 15). A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base today at 8:01 p.m. EDT (5:01 p.m. local time; 0001 GMT on Oct. 16), rising into clear blue skies above the Golden State's central coast. Such visibly striking launches are far from guaranteed; Vandenberg and its scenic surroundings are often blanketed by fog, making rocket watching in the area a dicey proposition. The Falcon 9's first stage rests on the deck of a drone ship shortly after launching the USSF-481 mission on Oct. 15, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) This evening's launch kicked off the USSF-481 mission, which is delivering mysterious payloads to an undisclosed location in the final frontier.
